mainTopic: Burning leftover limbs of Friday's תמיד on שבת or in טומאה: why רב הונא and רב חסדא rule differently, and a new מחלוקת about putting out the fire of the מחתה and מנורה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a מחלוקת about the leftover limbs of Friday's daily offering (תמיד). If they were not burned before שבת, or before the community became טמא, may they still be burned? רב הונא says they push aside טומאה but not שבת, because the end of a קרבן follows its beginning (סופו כתחילתו). רב חסדא rejects that rule. For him, שבת is fully permitted (הותרה) for a communal offering, so the limbs may be burned on שבת. טומאה is only pushed aside (דחויה), so only the main atonement stages may be done in טומאה, and the final burning may not. Next comes a new מחלוקת: is someone who puts out coals taken from the מזבח for the מחתה or the מנורה liable? אביי says חייב and רבא says פטור, and the גמרא gives two versions of exactly where they argue. In both versions, a ruling of רב נחמן is answered with one distinction: a coal taken off for no מצוה purpose is still altar fire, while the dispute is about a coal taken off for its מצוה. The amud ends with the הדרן closing פרק טרף בקלפי.

steps.title: Explaining the first view: the end of the offering follows its beginning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the first view (רב הונא). The start of a תמיד can be offered in טומאה, so its end can too. The start of a weekday תמיד can never be offered on שבת, so its end cannot either.
steps.simpleTranslation: With טומאה: the beginning of the offering is able to push aside טומאה, so its end also pushes it aside. With שבת: the beginning of a weekday offering is not able to push aside שבת, so its end also does not push it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why the first view (רב הונא) lets the leftover limbs be burned in טומאה but not on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is סופו כתחילתו: the last stage of a קרבן (burning the limbs) follows the same rules as its first stage (שחיטה and blood). A community תמיד may be started in טומאה, so it may be finished in טומאה. Friday's תמיד could never be started on שבת, because it belongs to Friday, so it cannot be finished on שבת either.

keyTerms.meaning: Its beginning (the first stages of the offering)
Its end (the final burning of the limbs)
Able to be pushed aside / able to override

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שבת is 'stronger' than טומאה in general. The point here is only that a *Friday* offering could never have been started on שבת. That is why its end cannot be done on שבת either.

phrases.aramaic: טוּמְאָה, דִּתְחִילָּתוֹ בַּר מִידְחֵא טוּמְאָה הוּא —
phrases.english: Impurity: since its beginning is able to override impurity —
phrases.notes: A communal תמיד may be slaughtered and offered even in טומאה.

phrases.english: its end also overrides.
phrases.notes: So the leftover limbs may also be burned in טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת, דִּתְחִילָּתוֹ לָאו בַּר מִידְחֵא שַׁבָּת הוּא —
phrases.english: Shabbat: since its beginning is not able to override Shabbat —
phrases.notes: A Friday תמיד can never be slaughtered on שבת.

phrases.english: its end also does not override.
phrases.notes: So Friday's leftover limbs may not be burned on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָה, דִּתְחִילָּתוֹ בַּר מִידְחֵא טוּמְאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the first view from the previous lines of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the view using the principle סופו כתחילתו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the two prohibitions should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of the offering follows its beginning. טומאה can be pushed aside at the beginning, so also at the end. שבת cannot be pushed aside at the beginning of a Friday offering, so also not at the end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover Friday limbs override טומאה but not שבת.

steps.title: רב חסדא rejects the 'end follows beginning' rule: שבת is fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's view is no problem either. He does not accept סופו כתחילתו. For a communal offering שבת is completely permitted (הותרה), so the end may be done on שבת as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב חסדא it is not difficult. He does not hold that the end is like the beginning. שבת is completely permitted for a communal offering, so the end also overrides it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second view, רב חסדא's, and shows why he allows burning the limbs on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not use the rule סופו כתחילתו at all. In his view, a communal offering does not just 'push aside' שבת. For such an offering, שבת is fully permitted (הותרה). So there is no reason to hold back from burning the limbs on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult / there is no problem
Its end is like its beginning (a principle)
He does not hold of it

phrases.english: According to Rav Ḥisda it is not difficult:
he does not hold that its end is like its beginning.
phrases.notes: The word in parentheses is a textual variant/duplication in the printed text.

phrases.english: Shabbat, which is fully permitted for the community —
its end also overrides.
phrases.notes: So the leftover limbs may be burned on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the opposite view, after the reasoning for the first view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the principle the first view relied on and substitutes the distinction between הותרה and דחויה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רב חסדא must also accept סופו כתחילתו, which would make his view hard to explain.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא does not accept סופו כתחילתו. Because שבת is הותרה for the community, even the end of the offering is done on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover limbs override שבת, because שבת is הותרה בציבור.

steps.title: Why רב חסדא does not let the end override טומאה
steps.stepSummary: For the community, טומאה is only pushed aside (דחויה), not fully permitted. So only the essential atonement stages override it. The final burning is not essential, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But טומאה is only pushed aside for the community. So its beginning, which is the main atonement, overrides; its end, which is not the main atonement, does not override.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רב חסדא by showing why טומאה is treated differently from שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is only דחויה is allowed only when truly necessary. The beginning of the offering (שחיטה and sprinkling the blood) brings the main atonement (עיקר כפרה), so it may be done in טומאה. Burning the limbs does not bring atonement, so it is not necessary enough to override טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushed aside (allowed only when necessary, not fully permitted)
The essential part that brings atonement

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the end follows the beginning, so the limbs override טומאה but not שבת. רב חסדא: שבת is הותרה, so the limbs override it. טומאה is only דחויה, so only the essential atonement stages override it, and the final burning does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: The distinction between טומאה הותרה בציבור and טומאה דחויה בציבור is a famous dispute that comes up across ש״ס. Here it decides whether non-essential parts of a קרבן may be done.

phrases.english: Impurity, which is only overridden for the community,
its beginning, which is the essential atonement — overrides,
phrases.notes: שחיטה and sprinkling of the blood.

phrases.aramaic: סוֹפוֹ דְּלָאו עִיקַּר כַּפָּרָה — לָא דָּחֵי.
phrases.english: its end, which is not the essential atonement — does not override.
phrases.notes: Burning the limbs on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's reasoning by contrasting טומאה with שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between essential and non-essential stages of the offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the beginning may be done in טומאה, one might think the end may be too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because טומאה is only דחויה, only the stages of עיקר כפרה override it. The final burning does not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover limbs do not override טומאה.

steps.title: New dispute: putting out the fire of the coal pan or the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת is stated. Someone puts out the fire of coals taken for the מחתה (the incense) or for lighting the מנורה. אביי says he is חייב. רבא says he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who extinguishes the fire of the מחתה (coal pan) or of the מנורה — אביי said: he is liable; רבא said: he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, a disagreement between אביי and רבא. It sets up a discussion of their reasons in the lines that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids putting out the altar fire (לא תכבה). The question is whether coals taken off the altar, for the incense pan or to light the מנורה, still count as 'altar fire'. אביי says they do, so the person is liable. רבא says they do not, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute of אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about putting out a fire on שבת. It is about the special prohibition against putting out the fire of the מזבח, even on a weekday.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who extinguishes the fire of the coal pan or of the menorah,
phrases.notes: The coals were taken from the altar for these uses.

phrases.english: Abaye said: he is liable,
Rava said: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still connected to the theme of the altar fire and the Temple service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: one who extinguishes coals of the מחתה or מנורה is liable. רבא: he is exempt.

steps.title: Where they agree and where they argue
steps.stepSummary: Putting out the coal on top of the מזבח is חייב according to everyone. The מחלוקת is only when the coal was brought down to the ground and put out there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put it out on top of the altar, everyone agrees he is liable. They argue when he brought it down to the ground and put it out there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which case the מחלוקת of אביי and רבא is about. It shows where they agree and where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו of 'לא תכבה' speaks about the fire 'על המזבח', on the altar. So a coal put out while still on the מזבח is clearly included, and no one argues about it. The open question is a coal that has already left the מזבח and been brought down to the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: he brought it down to the ground

phrases.english: Where he put it out on the top of the altar,
everyone agrees that he is liable.
When they argue, it is where he brought it down to the ground and put it out.
phrases.notes: This is the exact case of the מחלוקת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת stated in step 4 down to one specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the מזבח everyone says חייב. The dispute is only about a coal brought down to the ground.

steps.title: The reasons of אביי and רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he is חייב because it is still fire of the מזבח. רבא says he is פטור because once the coal was removed, it no longer counts as altar fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: he is liable, because it is still altar fire. רבא said: he is exempt, because once he removed it, it is removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, a coal keeps its status as אש המזבח even after it leaves the מזבח. For רבא, taking the coal off cuts it off from the מזבח, so the לאו of putting out altar fire no longer applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: once he removed it, it is removed (it lost its altar status)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a removed coal is still אש המזבח. רבא: once it is removed, it is cut off from the מזבח.

phrases.english: Abaye said: He is liable,
it is the fire of the altar,
Rava said: He is exempt,
since he removed it, it is removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: חַיָּיב, אֵשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the two sides in the case defined in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: חייב, because the coal is still altar fire. רבא: פטור, because removing it ended its altar status.

steps.title: רב נחמן's ruling seems to follow only אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rules that someone who takes a coal down from the מזבח and puts it out is חייב. That sounds like אביי, but the הלכה usually follows רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: one who takes a coal down from the altar and puts it out is liable. Whose view is that? אביי's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with an outside ruling that seems to match only אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's case is a coal taken down from the מזבח and then put out, which is exactly the disputed case. He says חייב, so he seems to agree with אביי against רבא. That is hard, because in disputes between אביי and רבא the הלכה follows רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: one who takes down a coal
from on top of the altar

phrases.english: But this that Rav Nachman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
One who takes down a coal from upon the altar
and puts it out is liable,
whose view is this? Abaye's!
phrases.notes: The challenge is that the הלכה normally follows רבא, not אביי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses an outside ruling to challenge רבא's view from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a coal removed from the מזבח is no longer altar fire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן makes someone חייב for a coal taken down and put out. That matches only אביי, so it leaves רבא, whose view is normally the הלכה, standing against an accepted ruling.

steps.title: Removed for its מצוה versus removed for no reason
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's ruling can fit רבא too. In רב נחמן's case the coal was not taken off for its מצוה, so it stays altar fire. In the case of אביי and רבא, it was taken for its מצוה (the מחתה or the מנורה).
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבא. There, the coal was not removed for its מצוה. Here, it was removed for its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רב נחמן's case is different from the case of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule 'once removed, it is removed' applies only when the coal was taken off to do a מצוה with it, like the incense pan or lighting the מנורה. A coal taken down for no purpose was never really cut off from the מזבח, so it is still אש המזבח. So רבא can agree that one is חייב for it.

keyTerms.meaning: it was removed for its מצוה
there / here (the two cases being compared)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a coal stops being altar fire only when it is removed for its מצוה. A coal taken down for no purpose is still אש המזבח, and putting it out is חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא says every coal taken off the מזבח loses its status. Only a coal taken for its מצוה is 'removed'.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rava,
there it was not removed for its מצוה,
here it was removed for its מצוה.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the coals taken for the מחתה or the מנורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by pointing to a difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by the purpose of removal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's ruling fits only אביי, which would put it against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both can fit רבא. A coal taken for its מצוה is cut off from the מזבח, but a coal taken for no reason stays altar fire.

steps.title: Opening a second version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that some report the dispute in a different way.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to give a second version of how the dispute between אביי and רבא was taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is decided here yet. The line only signals that the next lines will present the dispute in another form.

keyTerms.meaning: there are those who say (another version)

phrases.english: There are those who say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the first version and introduces a second version of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a second version of the מחלוקת, which continues next.

steps.title: In the second version, putting out the coal on the ground is exempt for everyone
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, everyone agrees that putting out the coal after it was brought down to the ground is פטור. The מחלוקת is only when the coal was put out on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he brought it down to the ground and put it out, everyone agrees he is exempt. When do they argue? Where he put it out on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second version of the dispute and first sets up where the argument is and where it is not. It is preparing for the two opinions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the first version. There, putting out the coal on top of the מזבח was חייב according to everyone, and the argument was about the ground. Here, the ground is פטור according to everyone, and the argument moves to the top of the מזבח, about a coal already taken off the fire for its מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (literally: all the world does not argue)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions! In the first version the top of the מזבח was חייב for everyone. In this version the ground is פטור for everyone. The place of the argument has flipped.

phrases.english: Where he brought it down to the ground and extinguished it,
everyone agrees that he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Once the coal is on the ground, it is no longer treated as altar fire in this version.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, דְּכַבְּיַּיהּ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: When they argue, it is where he extinguished it on top of the altar,
phrases.notes: This means after it was taken off the fire for its מצוה (into the מחתה), while still standing up on the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַחֲתַיהּ אַאַרְעָא וְכַבְּיַיהּ, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second version that step 9 announced, and flips the framing given in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second version, a coal put out on the ground is פטור according to everyone. The argument is only about a coal put out on top of the מזבח.

steps.title: אביי says liable, רבא says exempt, for a coal put out on top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he is חייב because it is still אש המזבח. רבא says he is פטור because once the coal was taken off the fire, it counts as removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He is liable, because it is still fire of the מזבח. רבא said: He is exempt, because once he removed it, it is removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the two opinions in the case that is under dispute in the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that while the coal is still up on the מזבח, it keeps its status as altar fire, even though it was taken out for its מצוה. רבא holds that the act of taking it off the fire ends its status as altar fire, even though it never left the top of the מזבח. So רבא is now more lenient than in the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire of the altar (which the תורה forbids putting out)
Once he removed it, it is removed (its status is cut off)

phrases.english: Abaye said: He is liable,
it is still fire of the altar,
Rava said: He is exempt,
once he has removed it, it is removed.
phrases.notes: Taking it off the fire for its מצוה cuts it off from being altar fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: חַיָּיב, אֵשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הוּא, רָבָא אָמַר: פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two sides of the argument that step 10 located on top of the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a coal put out on top of the מזבח after being taken out for its מצוה: אביי says חייב, רבא says פטור.

steps.title: רב נחמן's ruling seems to match neither אביי nor רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rules that someone who takes a coal down from the מזבח and puts it out is חייב. In the second version, nobody makes that person חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then this ruling, that רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: 'One who takes a coal down from the מזבח and puts it out is liable.' Whose opinion does it follow? It follows neither אביי nor רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version. It brings רב נחמן's ruling, which does not seem to fit either opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן makes the person חייב even after the coal was taken down from the מזבח. But in this version everyone agrees that a coal brought down to the ground is פטור. So even אביי, the stricter one, never says חייב once the coal is off the מזבח. That leaves רב נחמן with nobody to agree with.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither like this one nor like that one

steps.confusionAlert: In step 7 the problem was only with רבא (רב נחמן seemed to match אביי). Here it is worse: רב נחמן seems to match neither of them.

phrases.english: But this that Rav Naḥman said
in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
One who takes down a coal from upon the altar
and extinguishes it is liable,
according to whom?
Neither like Abaye nor like Rava!
phrases.notes: In this version both agree that a coal taken down to the ground is פטור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second version (steps 10-11) against רב נחמן's ruling, as step 7 did for the first version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of the אביי–רבא dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן makes a person חייב for a coal taken down from the מזבח. In this version everyone says a coal on the ground is פטור, so his ruling matches no opinion.

steps.title: רב נחמן's coal was not taken out for its מצוה
steps.stepSummary: In רב נחמן's case the coal was not taken off for its מצוה, so it stays altar fire even on the ground. אביי and רבא are talking about a coal taken off for its מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (רב נחמן's case), it was not taken out for its מצוה. Here (the dispute of אביי and רבא), it was taken out for its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that רב נחמן is talking about a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coal taken off for no מצוה purpose stays אש המזבח wherever it goes, so putting it out is חייב even on the ground. Only a coal taken out for its מצוה (like for the מחתה) loses that status, and that is the case of the dispute. So רב נחמן's ruling does not clash with either אביי or רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was removed for its מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the key is why the coal was taken off. A coal taken off for no מצוה reason stays altar fire. A coal taken off for its מצוה is the case where אביי and רבא argue.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same distinction answers the question in both versions. This shows that the 'removed for its מצוה' idea is the main point of the whole סוגיא.

phrases.english: There, it was not removed for its מצוה,
phrases.notes: רב נחמן's case: the coal stays altar fire even after being taken down.

phrases.english: here, it was removed for its מצוה.
phrases.notes: The case of אביי and רבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא אִינְּתִיק לְמִצְוָתַהּ, הָכָא אִינְּתִיק לְמִצְוָתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 with the same distinction used in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two rulings are about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's ruling clashes with both אביי and רבא in the second version.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן is talking about a coal not removed for its מצוה, which stays altar fire even on the ground. The dispute is only about a coal removed for its מצוה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק טרף בקלפי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the פרק of טרף בקלפי with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק טרף בקלפי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the formal closing line of the פרק. It is not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the fourth פרק of מסכת יומא, which dealt with the lottery for the goats and the service of the coals and incense. The next פרק will begin a new topic.

He shook the lottery box (the name of this פרק)
